info.title: VPNDetection API
info.description:
The VPNDetection API: classify any IP address, and download the databases
behind the answers.

See https://docs.vpndetection.io for guides and https://github.com/vpndetection-io
for the official client libraries.

tags.name: Database
tags.description: List and download the licensed databases.

tags.name: Entitlement

get.description:
Answers what is known about a single IPv4 or IPv6 address. Which fields
come back is decided by the plan behind the presented key; with no key
the answer is `ip` and `is_vpn`.

parameters.name: ip
parameters.description: The IPv4 or IPv6 address to classify.

200.description:
The classification. Present fields are those your plan includes; see
the tier table in the API description.

free.summary: No API key, or a key on the free plan

starter.summary: A key on the starter plan

scale.summary: A key on the scale plan, which adds the classification detail objects and the proxy FLAGS - the proxy detail stays on max

max.summary: A key on the max plan, address found in the VPN dataset

bogon.summary: A private address on the max plan, answered without a lookup

400.description: The path segment is not a valid IP address.

401.description: The presented API key is unknown, revoked, or expired.

403.description:
The key restricts which source addresses may use it, and this
request did not come from one of them.

example.error: source address not allowed for this API key

429.description:
Either a transient rate limit or a spent allowance. `Retry-After` is
present for the former and absent for the latter, and is the only
way to tell them apart.

Retry-After.description:
Seconds to wait before retrying. Present ONLY when the rejection
is a transient rate limit; its absence means an allowance is
spent and retrying will not help.

keylessDailyLimit.summary: Keyless daily cap spent, no Retry-After

value.error: daily limit for unauthenticated requests exceeded; use an API key
request allowance exceeded; raise or remove your overage limit

500.description: The VPN dataset could not be consulted.

get.description:
Answers what is known about the address this request came from, which is
the same answer `GET /{ip}` gives for that address: the plan behind the
presented key decides which fields come back, and the request counts
against the same allowance.

The address is the one our edge observed, so a request through a proxy
or a VPN reports the exit it left through rather than the machine that
made it. That is usually the point of asking.

200.description:
The classification of your own address. Present fields are those
your plan includes; see the tier table in the API description.

free.summary: No API key, or a key on the free plan

401.description: The presented API key is unknown, revoked, or expired.

403.description:
The key restricts which source addresses may use it, and this
request did not come from one of them.

example.error: source address not allowed for this API key

429.description:
Either the request rate was too high, or an allowance is spent.
The two are told apart by the message, not the status.

value.error: daily limit for unauthenticated requests exceeded; use an API key
request allowance exceeded; raise or remove your overage limit

500.description: The VPN dataset could not be consulted.

post.description:
Answers up to 1000 addresses in one call. Each distinct string in `ips`
is one lookup: it costs exactly what `GET /{ip}` costs for that address
and comes back with exactly the fields that call would carry for your
plan. Exact duplicates collapse to one entry and one lookup.

Both maps in the answer are keyed by the string you sent, so nothing has
to be lined up by position; the `ip` inside each result is the
normalized form. An address that could not be answered sits in `errors`
with the status and message the single lookup would have given, and
never disturbs the others: a string that is not an address is a `400`
there, and an allowance that runs out part way through leaves the
remaining entries as `429`s.

The call itself fails only for the reasons below, and a `429` on the
call always carries `Retry-After`: the batch is admitted or refused
whole by the rate limit, so a per-entry `429` is always a spent
allowance and never a throttle.

200.description:
One entry per distinct input string, in `results` or in `errors`.
Present fields within a result are those your plan includes; see the
tier table in the API description.

free.summary: No API key, or a key on the free plan

keylessDailyLimit.summary: No API key, and the daily allowance ran out after the first entry

8.8.8.8.error: daily limit for unauthenticated requests exceeded; use an API key

quotaExceeded.summary: A key on the starter plan whose allowance ran out after the first entry

8.8.8.8.error: request allowance exceeded; raise or remove your overage limit

lookupFailed.summary: The VPN dataset could not be consulted, which fails every entry

400.description: The body is not a batch, or names too few or too many addresses.

value.error: body must be a JSON object whose ips member is an array of strings
ips must hold between 1 and 1000 addresses

401.description: The presented API key is unknown, revoked, or expired.

403.description:
The key restricts which source addresses may use it, and this
request did not come from one of them.

example.error: source address not allowed for this API key

413.description: The body is larger than any batch of 1000 addresses can be.

429.description:
The rate limit refused the whole call. Always transient and always
with `Retry-After`; a spent allowance is reported per entry in a
`200` instead.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before retrying the call.

get.description:
Every database this organization may SEE, with where its licence stands.
Not just the ones you hold: a customer with one grant should be able to
tell what else is published without asking. `standing` is the
difference - `licensed`, `expired`, or `unlicensed` for one never
bought.
Answers `302` with a time-limited URL pointing straight at object storage. Follow the redirect; the link authorizes the START of a transfer, so one already running is not interrupted when it lapses.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description:
Not every database is built in every format. The `_provider`
catalogues are keyed by provider id rather than by IP range, so no
MMDB exists for them.

302.description: Follow the Location header to object storage

400.description: The database is not built in the requested format

403.description: Your organization holds no license for this database, or its term has ended

503.description: Licensed, but today's copy has not been published yet

get.description:
Poll this to decide whether today's build is worth fetching: it carries
`updated` and `entries` without downloading anything.

No `format` parameter - one document describes every format the database
is built in.
Checksums for one published file, so a download can be verified after it lands.

400.description: The database is not built in the requested format

get.description: Recent download attempts for this organization, newest first. Refusals are listed too, so a failed transfer can be accounted for.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many attempts to return. Clamped to 1 through 200.

get.description:
Answers what the presented key is, what plan is behind it, and what has
been spent against that plan's allowance in the current window.

paid.summary: A key on a paid plan, uncapped

free.summary: A key on the free plan. There is no subscription, so the window is the calendar month, and the allowance is a hard stop rather than a billable overage.

401.description: No key was presented, or it is unknown, revoked or expired.

403.description:
The key restricts which source addresses may use it, and this
request did not come from one of them.

example.error: source address not allowed for this API key

503.description:
The usage counters could not be read. Reported rather than guessed
at: the whole answer is the number, and a confident zero would read
as "you have used nothing".

get.description:
The identity behind this credential: what it is, the organization it is
scoped to, and the scopes it currently holds.

`user` is present for an OAuth token and ABSENT for an API key, which
has an organization but no person behind it. `credential.kind` says
which you are holding, so a client can branch without guessing from a
missing field.

Narrower than what the console shows its own user on purpose: an
integration needs a name to display and an organization to address, not
a profile. The `scopes` array is what the credential may do RIGHT NOW,
so a client can render its own capabilities rather than discovering
them from a 403.

The organization this credential is scoped to.

There is no way to name a different one. A credential describes exactly
one organization, so an identifier in the path could only ever be your
own or a refusal.

Read-only. Adding or removing a member is an invitation flow with email
in the middle rather than a POST, and modelling it as one here would
promise something this API does not do.

Metadata only. A key's secret is never in a list - not here and not in
the console - because a list is the response that ends up in logs,
caches and support tickets.

`retrievable` says whether the secret could still be read back at all.
A key issued before this product stored secrets recoverably was never
kept, so `reveal` will refuse it permanently; rotating produces one
that can be read.

post.description:
Creates a key and returns its secret.

This is the ONLY response that ever carries the secret, and only
because this is the moment it comes into existence. Store it now.

200.description: The new key, including its secret.

post.description:
Replaces the secret behind a key, keeping its id, name and settings.
The previous secret stops working immediately.

200.description: The key, with its new secret.

post.description:
Stops the key working. Revocation is soft: the key stays listed with a
`revoked_at`, because the organization still owns whatever it did while
it was alive.

Returns an existing key's secret.

Its own scope rather than part of `apikeys.manage`, because the two are
different acts: rotating replaces a secret you never see, while this
hands one over.

Refused with `NOT_RETRIEVABLE` for a key issued before this product
stored secrets recoverably - that secret was never kept, so no retry
will ever produce it. Rotate the key instead.

404.description:
No such key in this organization, or its secret was never stored
recoverably (`NOT_RETRIEVABLE`).

get.description:
RFC 8414 authorization server metadata: the endpoints, the grant types
and the scopes this server supports.

Read this rather than hardcoding endpoints. It is also served at
`/.well-known/openid-configuration`, identically, because several
clients probe that path first.

post.description:
Starts the device flow. Show the `user_code` to the person and send them
to `verification_uri`; `verification_uri_complete` has the code already
embedded, which is what to open if you can open a browser at all.

Then poll `/oauth/token`, no faster than `interval` seconds.

400.description:
`invalid_request`, `unauthorized_client` when the client may not use
the device flow, or `slow_down` when this address has started too
many authorizations.

get.description:
The browser entry point for the authorization-code flow. This is a
redirect target, not something to call from code.

An unknown `client_id` or an unregistered `redirect_uri` is shown to the
USER and never redirected, because sending an error to an address we
have not verified belongs to you is how an open redirector works.
Everything else comes back to your `redirect_uri` with `error`, your
`state`, and `iss`.

parameters.name: code_challenge_method
parameters.description: S256 only. `plain` is refused rather than downgraded.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: Returned unchanged. Use it to bind the response to your request.

parameters.name: resource
parameters.description: RFC 8707. What the token is FOR, so it cannot be replayed elsewhere.

302.description: A redirect to the consent screen, or back to your redirect_uri with an error.

400.description: Shown to the user. An unverified redirect target is never sent an error.

post.description:
Three grant types.

`urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:device_code` polls a device
authorization. Until the person approves it answers
`authorization_pending`; poll faster than `interval` and it answers
`slow_down`, which means widen your interval and keep it widened.

`authorization_code` exchanges a code from `/oauth/authorize`, with the
`code_verifier` matching the challenge you sent.

`refresh_token` exchanges a refresh token. The presented token is
consumed whatever happens next, so store the new one before using it.

400.description:
An RFC 6749 error. `authorization_pending` and `slow_down` are
normal answers while polling a device authorization, not failures.
`access_denied` means the person refused, and `expired_token` that
the device code is no longer valid: it expired, or it was already
exchanged or refused. `invalid_grant` means the code, device code or
refresh token is not valid for this `client_id`. `slow_down` also
answers any grant when this address sends too many requests.

post.description:
RFC 7009. Always answers 200, including for a token that was never
valid - an endpoint that distinguished the two would be a way to test
whether a stolen string is a live credential.

Revoking a REFRESH token ends the whole authorization and takes its
access tokens with it. Revoking an access token affects only that token.

apiKeyQuery.name: apikey
apiKeyQuery.description: `?apikey=<key>`. Convenient in a browser; prefer a header elsewhere.

LookupResponse.description:
The union of every plan's answer. Only `ip` and `is_vpn` are guaranteed;
each remaining field is present when your plan includes it, and absent
otherwise. A client that must work across plans should treat an absent
flag as unknown rather than as `false`.

ip.description: The address that was looked up, normalized.

is_vpn.description:
Whether the address is VPN infrastructure. Keys off presence in the
VPN dataset, so an unattributed range with no provider is still
`true`.

is_hosting.description: Whether the address belongs to a hosting or cloud provider. Starter and above.

is_relay.description: Whether the address is a privacy relay egress. Starter and above.

is_tor.description: Whether the address is a Tor node. Starter and above.

is_cdn.description: Whether the address belongs to a CDN. Starter and above.

is_resproxy.description: Whether the address was seen in a residential proxy pool. Scale and above.

is_dcproxy.description: Whether the address was seen in a datacenter proxy pool. Scale and above.

is_mobproxy.description: Whether the address was seen in a mobile proxy pool. Scale and above.

vpn.description: Detail for `is_vpn`. Empty when `is_vpn` is false. Starter and above.

hosting.description: Detail for `is_hosting`. Empty when false. Scale and above.

relay.description: Detail for `is_relay`. Empty when false. Scale and above.

tor.description:
Detail for `is_tor`. Empty when false. Scale and above. The tor
dataset carries no provider, so `provider` is always an empty string.

cdn.description: Detail for `is_cdn`. Empty when false. Scale and above.

resproxy.description: Detail for `is_resproxy`. Empty when false. Max only.

dcproxy.description: Detail for `is_dcproxy`. Empty when false. Max only.

mobproxy.description: Detail for `is_mobproxy`. Empty when false. Max only.

ips.description:
The addresses to classify, 1 to 1000 per call, counted before
duplicates collapse. Each distinct string is one lookup.

results.description:
One answer per input string that was classified, keyed by the string
as you sent it; the `ip` inside is the normalized form. Each value is
exactly what `GET /{ip}` answers for your plan.

errors.description:
One entry per input string that could not be classified, keyed the
same way. Empty when every entry was answered.

BatchLookupError.description: Why one entry of a batch was not answered, as the single lookup would have reported it.

status.description:
The HTTP status `GET /{ip}` would have answered for this entry: `400`
for a string that is not an address, `429` for a spent allowance,
`500` when the VPN dataset could not be consulted. A `429` here is
never a throttle; the whole call is refused instead.

error.description: The same message the single lookup carries for that status.

VpnDetail.description:
What is known about the VPN attribution. Every key is present when the
object is populated, empty values included; the object is `{}` when
`is_vpn` is false. `confidence` and `method` are max only, so on a lower
plan they are absent from a populated object rather than empty.

provider.description: The VPN provider, or an empty string for an unattributed range.

last_seen.description: The most recent date this address was observed as VPN infrastructure.

confidence.description: How strongly the attribution is supported. Max only.

method.description:
The class of evidence the attribution rests on, one of four values.
Max only.

`scan` - we spoke the VPN protocol to the address ourselves and got a
valid server response. `scrape` - the operator published the address
through its own API, client or configuration. `registry` - public
registration or naming records attribute it to the operator.
`infer` - the address was extrapolated from confirmed neighbours in
the same block.

ClassDetail.description:
The shared detail shape for the hosting, relay, tor and cdn datasets.
Every key is present when the object is populated; the object is `{}`
when its flag is false.

provider.description: The provider, or an empty string where the dataset has none.

confidence.description: How strongly the classification is supported.

last_seen.description: The most recent date this address was observed in this dataset.

ProxyDetail.description:
The shared detail shape for the residential, datacenter and mobile proxy
families, measured over a rolling 90 day window. Every key is present
when the object is populated; the object is `{}` when its flag is false.

provider.description: The proxy network, or an empty string where unattributed.

first_seen.description: The earliest date within the window this address was seen in the pool.

last_seen.description: The most recent date within the window this address was seen in the pool.

hits.description: How many times the address was observed in the pool during the window.

hits_days_pct.description:
The share of days in the window on which the address was seen, as a
percentage. A high value means a stable pool member rather than a
one-off sighting.

providers_num.description: How many distinct proxy networks this address was seen in.

LookupError.description: Every non-2xx response carries this shape.

error.description: A human-readable explanation of the failure.

Standing.description:
Where your license for a database family stands today. `licensed` is a
live grant, `expired` one whose term has ended, and `unlicensed` a
database published but never bought.

DatabaseFormat.description: A file format a database version is published in.

bytes.description:
Size of the published file, or null when it has not been published
yet. int64 because it is not hypothetical: resproxy_ip_14d's MMDB is
4.58 GB, so a 32-bit field cannot carry the catalogue and `list`
throws for every caller rather than for that one entry.

Database.description:
One database FAMILY your organization is licensed for. A license covers
the family, while a download names a specific version, so the ids you
pass to the download and checksum endpoints come from `versions`.

base.description: The database family, e.g. `vpn_ip`. What the license is held against.

license_type.description:
What a license permits you to do with the data. Null for a family
you hold no license for, which is every one with standing
`unlicensed`.

expires.description: A hard stop. Null when the license has no end date, which is the normal case for a rolling agreement, and when there is no license. A rolling license reports its turnover date in renews_at instead.

renews_at.description: When a rolling license next renews. Null when the license has no defined term, when expires sets a hard stop instead, and when there is no license.

notice_due_at.description: The last day notice of non-renewal can be given for the term ending at renews_at. Null whenever renews_at is, and when the agreement records no notice period.

in_term.description: False when the license has lapsed; downloads are refused.

versions.description:
Every published version of this family. The `id` here is what the
download and checksum endpoints take.

id.description: The versioned database id, e.g. `vpn_ip_v1`. Pass this to download.

sample_formats.description: The formats an evaluation sample is published in, if any.

Download.description:
One download ATTEMPT, refusals included - a denial is what answers "it
stopped working", so they are listed rather than dropped.

sample.description: The evaluation sample rather than the database itself.

bytes.description:
Object size at redirect time, NOT bytes delivered: the transfer is a
presigned redirect straight to object storage, so we never observe it.
int64 for the same reason as DatabaseFormatSize.bytes - it is the
size of the same object.

apikey_id.description:
The key that made the request. Null when the org acted through the
console rather than through a key.

DbChecksums.description: The published digests for one database file.

update_freq.description: How often a new build is published

entries.description: Row count in the current build

sample.description: A few real rows, keyed by format

sample_size.description: Bytes per format of the evaluation sample, where one is published

sample_entries.description: Row count in the evaluation sample

org_id.description: The organization the key belongs to.

EntitlementApikey.description:
The credential itself. The key is never echoed - only its id, which is
what the console shows and what you can act on.

expires.description: Null for a key with no end date, which is the normal case.

allowed_cidrs.description:
The source addresses this key may be used from. EMPTY means
unrestricted, never "deny all".

key.description: The plan the organization is on.

tier.description:
The field tier, which decides how much of a lookup answer comes
back. What each tier includes is documented on the lookup endpoint
rather than repeated here, so there is one place it can be wrong.

requests.description:
Requests counted in the current window. The same number the lookup
API gates on, and it can lag by a few seconds.

quota.description: What the plan includes. Zero on a plan that includes none.

hard_limit.description:
Where we stop serving. NULL means never, which is the normal state
of an uncapped paid plan and is not the same as zero. Above the
quota and below this, requests are served and billed as overage.

window_start.description: When the current allowance period began.

rc.description: The outcome. `SUCCESS` on success; otherwise the reason.

scopes.description: What this credential may do right now.

ApikeyDetail.description: Key METADATA. Never the key itself.

key_prefix.description: The leading, non-secret part, so a key is recognisable without storing it.

allowed_cidrs.description: Source-IP allowlist. EMPTY MEANS UNRESTRICTED, not deny-all.

retrievable.description: Whether this key's secret can still be read back. False permanently for a key issued before secrets were stored recoverably.

name.description: A label you will recognise later. Shown wherever the key is listed.

allowed_scopes.description: What the new key may do. Omit for a key that carries no named scope, which is the safe default.

key.description: The secret. Returned once, here, and never again.

token_endpoint_auth_methods_supported.description: Always `none`. Every client is public and has no secret.

authorization_response_iss_parameter_sup.description: RFC 9207. A redirect back from the authorization endpoint carries `iss`.

scope.description: Space-delimited. Anything your client is not registered for is dropped rather than refused.

resource.description: RFC 8707: what the token is for.

device_code.description: Yours. Poll with it; never show it to anyone.

user_code.description: Short and typable. This is what the person confirms.

verification_uri_complete.description: The same page with the code already filled in.

device_code.description: Required by the device code grant.

code.description: Required by the authorization code grant.

code_verifier.description: Required by the authorization code grant.

redirect_uri.description: Authorization code grant: the `redirect_uri` the code was issued against, exactly.

refresh_token.description: Required by the refresh token grant.

expires_in.description: Seconds until the access token expires.

refresh_token.description: Always returned. A refresh consumes the token it presents, so keep this one.

scope.description: What was actually granted, which may be narrower than what was asked for.

mslm:apikey_id.description:
Not part of OAuth. The ID of the API key the person picked when they
approved, returned by every grant while this authorization may still
read that key back. Absent when no key was picked, or when the
person's role no longer allows reading keys back.

mslm:apikey.description:
Not part of OAuth. The API key itself, so a device ends up holding an
ordinary key. Returned by the device code and authorization code
grants only, never by a refresh, and only alongside
`mslm:apikey_id`. Absent when that key's secret cannot be read back,
which is the case for a key created before keys could be shown again
in the console; a rotated key can be.

token.description: An access token or a refresh token.

Unauthorized.description: Missing or invalid key, or the key lacks the db.download scope

NotLicensed.description: Your organization holds no license for this database, or its term has ended

NotAvailable.description: Licensed, but today's copy has not been published yet

AccountUnauthorized.description: No credential was presented, or it is not valid.

AccountForbidden.description:
The credential does not hold the scope this endpoint requires. The
missing scope is deliberately not named.

AccountNotFound.description: No such key in this organization.

AccountInvalid.description: The request body is missing a required field.

ApikeyIdParam.name: id
ApikeyIdParam.description: The key's id, as returned by the list endpoint. Never the key itself.
